extension.summary: Control your LAN smart home from inside Kodi
extension.description: Paragon Home is part of the Paragon TV project. It controls your LAN smart home from inside Kodi instead of a separate app per brand: Govee lights, Broadlink RM infrared blasters, Tuya smart plugs (GHome, Gosund, Smart Life) and TP-Link Kasa plugs.[CR][CR]Lights are driven over the Govee LAN API (UDP, no internet round-trip, no rate limit) whenever LAN Control is enabled on the device, and fall back to the Govee Cloud API when it is not. Power, brightness, RGB colour and colour temperature are all supported, along with named scenes you can build and re-use.[CR][CR]An optional background service syncs your lights to playback: dim when something starts, come part-way up on pause, and restore when playback stops. Every action is also reachable through RunScript() so it can be bound to a remote button or saved as a favourite.
extension.news: v2.24.0[CR]Satellite mode: one box keeps the setup and the others copy it, so a house with several Kodi boxes runs one schedule rather than three.[CR][CR]v2.23.1[CR]Plugs no longer appear in a scene's light list. Scenes are lights, everywhere and without exception.[CR][CR]v2.23.0[CR]A scene applied to "all" now means the lights. Plugs are only switched when named, and infrared blasters are no longer offered as scene targets at all.[CR][CR]v2.22.0[CR]A step can now pause for up to an hour, and the service keeps cycling and reacting to playback while it waits.[CR][CR]v2.21.1[CR]Switching the lights off, or any other bulk change, now stops a running colour cycle. Previously only applying a scene did, so a shutdown left the cycle ticking.[CR][CR]v2.21.0[CR]Scenes can hold a separate brightness for lightbars, so one figure no longer has to suit both a bar and a bulb.[CR][CR]v2.20.0[CR]Phase times now match Paragon TV, which computes them from an anchor and offsets rather than storing them.[CR][CR]v2.19.2[CR]The Paragon TV report now names the settings the installed build really uses.[CR][CR]v2.19.1[CR]A rerack can now report exactly what it reads from Paragon TV, and why that might be nothing.[CR][CR]v2.19.0[CR]The add-on id is now script.paragon.home. Everything saved under the old id is carried over.[CR][CR]v2.18.1[CR]Sequences can be duplicated too.[CR][CR]v2.18.0[CR]Scenes can be duplicated.[CR][CR]v2.17.0[CR]The weekly table can be matched to Paragon TV's and stays matched.[CR][CR]v2.16.0[CR]Each phase decides for itself whether to run with Paragon TV or at a time of its own.[CR][CR]v2.15.0[CR]Reracks: a day in nine phases, each holding a sequence, so one sequence can be used several times a day.[CR][CR]v2.14.0[CR]Reracks are now called sequences. Yours are carried over.[CR][CR]v2.13.0[CR]A rerack can follow one of Paragon TV's nine phases instead of its own clock.[CR][CR]v2.12.0[CR]Reracks can run themselves: a time and the days it applies to.[CR][CR]v2.11.0[CR]Scenes can send infrared commands, and Tuya plugs have a power-cut setting.[CR][CR]v2.10.1[CR]A colour scene no longer switches every plug in the house.[CR][CR]v2.10.0[CR]Reracks: ten ordered steps run as one, across every driver.[CR][CR]v2.9.0[CR]Says whether a Kasa plug actually used your TP-Link account, which explains some plugs working and others not.[CR][CR]v2.8.2[CR]Fixed an ascii codec error when switching a later Kasa plug.[CR][CR]v2.8.1[CR]A failure on any device was being explained as a Govee one. Each driver now reports its own reason.[CR][CR]v2.8.0[CR]Supports later Kasa hardware (HS103 v5 and similar), which speaks a different protocol and needs your TP-Link account under Settings.[CR][CR]v2.7.2[CR]The Kasa sweep was covering the wrong subnet. It now takes the range from devices known to be on the network.[CR][CR]v2.7.1[CR]Fixed a Kasa search finding only some of the plugs, and it now works on networks that drop broadcast.[CR][CR]v2.7.0[CR]TP-Link Kasa plugs (HS100, HS103, HS110, KP series). No account and no key -- run a device search and they appear.[CR][CR]v2.6.1[CR]Renamed the last of "Paragon Govee" to "Paragon Home". Your devices, scenes and colours are untouched.[CR][CR]v2.6.0[CR]The menu is now sorted by kind of device, and each one offers only what it can actually do.[CR][CR]v2.5.0[CR]Multi-outlet plugs get an "All outlets" entry that switches the whole box in one command.[CR][CR]v2.4.0[CR]Drives Tuya protocol 3.4, which negotiates a session key on every connection.[CR][CR]v2.3.0[CR]Tuya smart plugs can now be switched, not just found. Multi-outlet plugs are listed one device per outlet.[CR][CR]v2.2.2[CR]Dialogs say Paragon Home rather than Paragon Govee, and take the name from the add-on itself.[CR][CR]v2.2.1[CR]New Tuya search diagnostic: says whether the ports opened, what arrived, and why nothing was heard.[CR][CR]v2.2.0[CR]Finds Tuya smart plugs (GHome, Gosund, Smart Life). Switching them needs a local key from your Tuya account - discovery works without one.[CR][CR]v2.1.2[CR]Supports the newer Broadlink data framing used by RM4 and later RM Mini 3 units, and corrects itself if the guess is wrong.[CR][CR]v2.1.1[CR]Broadlink errors are now decoded into words. Error 0xffff means the device is locked in the Broadlink app.[CR][CR]v2.1.0[CR]Broadlink RM support: discovery, IR learning and sending, over the LAN with no cloud account.[CR][CR]v2.0.0[CR]Restructured around a driver interface so other LAN devices can be added. Govee is now the first driver; nothing about your lights, scenes or colours changes.[CR][CR]v1.7.1[CR]Cycle steps now send only the colour, and sends are paced across the lights.[CR][CR]v1.7.0[CR]Mix scenes can now cycle: every light moves to the next colour on a timer you choose.[CR][CR]v1.6.0[CR]New mix scenes: pick several colours and they are spread evenly but randomly over the lights, reshuffling each time.[CR][CR]v1.5.0[CR]The colour list is now yours to edit: add, rename, recolour, reorder and delete colours by hex code.[CR][CR]v1.4.0[CR]A light that misses one search now keeps its name instead of being erased. Added Forget this light.[CR][CR]v1.3.1[CR]Identify now flashes 10 times instead of 3, can be cancelled, and puts the light back as it was.[CR][CR]v1.3.0[CR]New Name lights one by one walkthrough: each light comes on bright magenta in turn while you type its name.[CR][CR]v1.2.0[CR]Colour entry now accepts the 8-digit hex codes the Govee app uses, and says how it read them.[CR][CR]v1.1.4[CR]New Check status reporting test: drives one bulb to a known colour and reads it back, to prove whether the model reports its state honestly.[CR][CR]v1.1.3[CR]A coloured bulb is no longer captured as white when a stale colour temperature sits beside it.[CR][CR]v1.1.2[CR]Capture fixes: brightness scale detection, no more long hang when bulbs are slow, and it now reports what it read.[CR][CR]v1.1.1[CR]Capture is now on the main menu, and the menu title shows the running version.[CR][CR]v1.1.0[CR]Capture the lights' current state as a scene - the way to bring a Govee Tap-to-Run into Kodi.[CR]Scenes can now hold a different setting per light.[CR][CR]v1.0.2[CR]LAN search now probes every network interface and falls back to broadcast.[CR]Added a Diagnose LAN search tool that says why a search found nothing.[CR][CR]v1.0.1[CR]Fixed the background service failing to start on Kodi 17.6 with "TypeError: an integer is required".[CR][CR]v1.0.0[CR]First release.[CR]LAN and Cloud transports with automatic per-device selection.[CR]Power, brightness, colour and colour temperature control.[CR]User-editable scenes.[CR]Playback-reactive lighting service.[CR]RunScript() actions for keymaps and favourites.
